stages.name: Find Opportunity
stages.desc: Identify relevant freelance opportunities, client briefs, and formal RFPs.

stages.name: Qualify
stages.desc: Evaluate skill fit, calendar capacity, delivery feasibility, and project risk.

stages.name: Research
stages.desc: Conduct ethical research into the client's business, products, audience, and market context.

stages.name: Clarify
stages.desc: Formulate targeted pre-proposal questions to eliminate ambiguities and unstated assumptions.

stages.name: Scope
stages.desc: Break down project tasks, itemize specific deliverables, and set explicit exclusions.

stages.name: Estimate

stages.name: Write

stages.name: Review

stages.name: Pitch

stages.name: Track
stages.desc: Monitor pipeline status across 10 stages in a structured tracking sheet.

why_now.industry_shift: Clients and marketplace algorithms heavily penalize generic AI-generated copy-paste proposals in favor of tailored diagnostic pitches.
why_now.ai_impact: AI tools accelerate research and outline drafting, but human empathy, commercial judgment, and bespoke project scoping win client trust.
why_now.business_demand: Clients receive dozens of low-effort spam bids and eagerly reward freelancers who demonstrate clear comprehension of their specific problem.
why_now.career_opportunity: Mastering proposal development, commercial estimation, and professional pitching empowers independent professionals to win better clients and protect profit margins.

responsible_ai_workflows.heading: Use AI to Refine Proposals. Keep Every Commercial Promise Verifiable.
responsible_ai_workflows.copy: Learn to use AI tools for proposal outlines, clearer writing, pricing assumptions and document review while maintaining professional judgment. Every claim, project estimate, credential and client commitment must be verified before a proposal is presented.
appropriate_uses: Brief summarization and key parameter extraction
Requirement categorization into mandatory and optional items
Generating structural proposal outlines tailored to the brief
Refining client problem statements for clarity and brevity
Editing tone for professional confidence and conciseness
Simplifying technical jargon for non-technical clients
Reviewing internal consistency across deliverables and pricing
Drafting objection-handling outlines and respectful follow-up messages
mandatory_human_checks: Candidate's genuine skills and capability match
Relevance and ownership of project portfolio samples
Applicable taxes, fees, and payment terms
Third-party software, asset, and licensing fees
Designated approval authority and sign-off process
prohibited_practices: Fabricating client research or market facts
Inventing previous client names or engagement history
Presenting unearned certificates or false credentials
Claiming nonexistent technical or creative capabilities
Inventing prices, discounts, or unauthorized delivery timelines
Uploading confidential client RFPs into unauthorized AI tools
Presenting AI hallucinations as researched facts
Sending automated, unreviewed proposals to clients
responsible_ai_workflows.safe_prompt_example: Review this fictional freelance proposal for clarity, relevance and commercial consistency. Use only the supplied client brief and verified service capabilities. Identify missing scope details, unclear deliverables, unsupported claims and pricing assumptions. Do not invent past projects, client results, deadlines, testimonials, commitments or costs.

coordination_framework.heading: Move Beyond Generic Bids. Build Proposals With Clear Scope, Evidence and Commercial Logic.
coordination_framework.pricing_formula_model: Labor Cost = Hours × Internal Rate; Base Cost = Labor Cost + Direct Expenses; Price with Markup = Cost × (1 + Markup); Price with Margin = Cost ÷ (1 − Margin).
coordination_framework.milestone_reconciliation: Every multi-phase project milestone reconciles deliverable evidence to payment stage amounts.
coordination_framework.sow_governance: A 14-section Statement of Work providing commercial clarity, deliverable specifications, and formal change-request procedures.

lessons.title: Understanding Freelance Opportunities
lessons.what_is_taught: Navigating freelance project categories: service-based contracts, small fixed-price assignments, multi-stage milestone projects, recurring retainer engagements, direct client inbound enquiries, client briefs, and formal RFPs.

lessons.title: Types of Client Briefs
lessons.what_is_taught: Deconstructing varied client briefs: informal messages, formal project briefs, job descriptions, Requests for Proposal (RFPs), Requests for Quotation (RFQs), creative briefs, and technical specifications.

lessons.title: Reading the Client Brief
lessons.what_is_taught: Extracting key brief parameters: project objective, underlying business problem, target audience, commercial context, required deliverables, delivery timelines, budget hints, required skills, and approval workflows.

lessons.title: Understanding Buyer Objectives
lessons.what_is_taught: Diagnosing buyer motives: business problems, commercial desired outcomes, operational bottlenecks, technical constraints, design requirements, service expectations, and explicit success criteria.

lessons.title: Requirements Analysis
lessons.what_is_taught: Categorizing project requirements: mandatory specifications, preferred features, optional enhancements, existing client assets, client dependencies, acceptance conditions, and missing information.

lessons.title: Opportunity Qualification
lessons.what_is_taught: Applying qualification filters: skill alignment, calendar availability, scope clarity, budget adequacy, delivery feasibility, client expectations, communication style, and potential project risk.

lessons.title: Feasibility Review
lessons.what_is_taught: Assessing operational feasibility: required labor effort, technical complexity, available tools, deadline constraints, external vendor dependencies, skills gaps, and licensing considerations.

lessons.title: Client Research
lessons.what_is_taught: Conducting public client research: official company websites, core products and services, public client portfolio, market positioning, industry vertical context, and project-specific business needs.
topics: Client public work and brand tone

lessons.title: Responsible Client Research
lessons.what_is_taught: Adhering to ethical research boundaries: respecting client privacy, avoiding unfounded assumptions, strictly refusing unauthorized scraping or confidential data gathering, and separating observed facts from interpretations.
topics: No confidential or private data collection

lessons.title: Clarification Questions
lessons.what_is_taught: Drafting targeted pre-proposal clarification inquiries: What problem needs solving? Who is the end user? What deliverables are required? What assets exist? What is the deadline? Who approves? What constraints exist?
topics: Who is the intended customer or user?
What is the firm target deadline?
Who has final project approval authority?
What is the expected review process?
What technical or budget constraints exist?

lessons.title: Risk Identification
lessons.what_is_taught: Spotting commercial and delivery red flags: ambiguous scopes, unreasonable turnaround times, unclear ownership, missing client assets, unapproved third-party content, budget volatility, and excessive revision demands.
topics: Ambiguous or shifting scope of work

lessons.title: Qualification Decision
lessons.what_is_taught: Making defensible bid/no-bid determinations: identifying suitable opportunities, flagging items requiring clarification, declining unfeasible briefs courteously, and referring to specialists when appropriate.
topics: When to request clarification before bidding

lessons.title: Opportunity Analysis Worksheet
lessons.what_is_taught: Completing the Opportunity Analysis Worksheet: brief summary, project category, objectives, deliverables breakdown, feasibility score, identified risks, open questions, and bid/no-bid recommendation.

modules.hands_on_lab: Analyze THREE realistic client briefs corresponding to: 1. Small fixed-price service, 2. Larger milestone-based project, 3. Recurring service engagement. Identify different scope and pricing considerations.
modules.practical_assignment: Create an Opportunity Qualification & Client Brief Analysis worksheet for all three cases.
modules.expected_deliverable: Three Client Brief Analysis Sheets and a Qualification Matrix
modules.commercial_application: Helps freelancers and agencies avoid unsuitable opportunities and prepare more relevant proposals.

modules.title: Proposal Structure & Persuasive Writing
modules.name: Proposal Structure & Persuasive Writing
modules.module_purpose: Create clear, customized and evidence-based proposals that help clients understand the recommended solution.
modules.objective: Create clear, customized and evidence-based proposals that help clients understand the recommended solution.

lessons.title: Purpose of a Professional Proposal
lessons.what_is_taught: Distinguishing proposals from simple price quotations, casual pitches, and legal Statements of Work; supporting client decision-making with commercial clarity and professional tone.
topics: Proposal vs price quotation vs pitch

lessons.title: Proposal Formats
lessons.what_is_taught: Selecting proposal formats: short direct freelance proposal, formal service proposal, comprehensive project proposal, agency proposal, retainer proposal, and formal RFP responses.

lessons.title: Personalized Openings
lessons.what_is_taught: Writing relevant, personalized openings: demonstrating client-specific context, acknowledging core requirements, framing the problem accurately, and eliminating generic filler.
topics: Eliminating generic greetings and boilerplate filler

lessons.title: Proposal Length
lessons.what_is_taught: Matching proposal length to project complexity: short proposals for simple tasks, detailed proposals for complex engagements, adhering to RFP guidelines, and avoiding artificial word counts.
topics: Short proposals for clearly defined jobs

lessons.title: Client Problem Statement
lessons.what_is_taught: Articulating the client problem: stated challenges, business context, desired outcomes, operational friction, missing information, and avoiding invented problems.

lessons.title: Proposed Solution
lessons.what_is_taught: Designing the proposed solution: service approach, work phases, execution methods, key deliverables, practical rationale, constraints, and project outputs.

lessons.title: Scope Presentation
lessons.what_is_taught: Presenting scope transparently: included tasks, deliverables inventory, deliverable quantities, delivery formats, technical specifications, review stages, and explicit exclusions.

lessons.title: Relevant Proof of Capability
lessons.what_is_taught: Selecting genuine evidence: past project examples, portfolio case studies, technical methods, demonstrated achievements, and verifiable client results.

lessons.title: Evidence for New Freelancers
lessons.what_is_taught: Presenting proof without prior client history: original sample work, academic projects, training assignments, personal side projects, volunteer work, and accurately labeling practice work.
topics: Ethical labeling of simulated vs paid client work

lessons.title: Proposal Benefits
lessons.what_is_taught: Translating features into client value: problem-solution alignment, practical business outcomes, delivery efficiency, client convenience, and quality standards.

lessons.title: Project Methodology
lessons.what_is_taught: Outlining project execution phases: discovery, planning, execution, review, revisions, and handover; scaling methodology to project scope.

lessons.title: Credible Timelines
lessons.what_is_taught: Constructing realistic timelines: planned activities, client dependencies, review turnarounds, milestone dates, contingency buffers, and assumptions without false deadline guarantees.
topics: Identifying client dependencies and input times

lessons.title: Proposal Pricing Presentation
lessons.what_is_taught: Formatting proposal prices clearly: service description, pricing basis (fixed vs hourly vs milestone), included scope, optional add-ons, payment stages, currency, and tax treatment.
topics: Detailing included work in each package

lessons.title: Calls to Action
lessons.what_is_taught: Formulating low-friction next steps: scheduling clarification calls, confirming project scope, reviewing draft proposals, requesting formal sign-off, and aligning CTAs to decision stages.
topics: Matching CTA to client decision stage

lessons.title: Professional Proposal Formatting
lessons.what_is_taught: Designing readable documents: clear heading hierarchies, balanced white space, readable typography, structured comparison tables, visual branding, and accessible PDF exports.
topics: Structured tables for deliverables and prices
Consistent page layouts and clean PDF export

lessons.title: Proposal Customization
lessons.what_is_taught: Adapting proposals to client contexts: small business vs enterprise, technical vs creative briefs, matching information density, and stripping out irrelevant boilerplate.
topics: Direct inquiries vs formal RFP responses

lessons.title: AI-Assisted Proposal Writing
lessons.what_is_taught: Leveraging AI responsibly: outline ideation, problem statement drafting, tone editing, conciseness editing, proofreading, and mandatory human verification of claims.
topics: Mandatory human verification of all facts

lessons.title: Proposal Quality Checklist
lessons.what_is_taught: Auditing proposals against quality rubrics: factual accuracy, brief relevance, deliverable specificity, genuine evidence, pricing transparency, realistic timelines, and appropriate CTAs.

modules.commercial_application: Direct freelance enquiries, agency proposals, consulting services and project-based client engagements.

modules.title: Pricing & Scope of Work
modules.name: Pricing & Scope of Work
modules.module_purpose: Estimate project work, calculate defensible prices and define clear commercial scope and responsibilities.
modules.objective: Estimate project work, calculate defensible prices and define clear commercial scope and responsibilities.

lessons.title: Pricing Fundamentals
lessons.what_is_taught: Understanding commercial pricing principles: cost vs price vs value, labor effort estimation, project risk premiums, profit margins, freelance capacity, client budgets, and market positioning.

lessons.title: Hourly Pricing
lessons.what_is_taught: Calculating defensible hourly rates: target annual income, billable vs non-billable hours, direct business expenses, platform fees, buffer contingencies, and rate rounding.

lessons.title: Fixed-Price Estimation
lessons.what_is_taught: Building fixed-price project estimates: Work Breakdown Structure (WBS), task-level effort estimation, internal hourly cost, direct expenses, client review time, revision allowance, and profit margins.

lessons.title: Pricing Formula — Basic Cost Model
lessons.what_is_taught: Applying core mathematical cost models: Labor Cost = Estimated Hours × Internal Hourly Cost; Estimated Base Cost = Labor Cost + Direct Expenses + Other Project Costs.
topics: Labor Cost formula: Hours × Internal Rate
Distinguishing internal cost from client price

lessons.title: Markup vs Profit Margin
lessons.what_is_taught: Mastering the mathematical difference between markup and profit margin: Selling Price with Markup = Cost × (1 + Markup Rate); Selling Price for Target Gross Margin = Cost ÷ (1 − Target Margin Rate).
topics: Selling Price with Markup formula: Cost × (1 + Markup)
Selling Price for Target Margin formula: Cost ÷ (1 − Margin)
Comparing numerical differences between markup and margin

lessons.title: Pricing Calculator in Google Sheets
lessons.what_is_taught: Developing a functional pricing calculator in Google Sheets: hours input, internal hourly cost, labor cost formula, direct expenses, contingency rates, target markup/margin options, and proposal selling prices.
topics: Labor cost formulas and dynamic references
Direct expenses and asset line items

lessons.title: Calculation Validation
lessons.what_is_taught: Validating spreadsheet models: formula audits, catching divide-by-zero errors, preventing invalid negative inputs, percentage formatting, avoiding double-counted costs, and scenario stress testing.

lessons.title: Fixed-Price Project Scope
lessons.what_is_taught: Defining fixed-price project scope: included activities, deliverables count, technical formats, review milestones, acceptance criteria, and explicit non-negotiable boundaries.
topics: Inventory of included tasks and activities

lessons.title: Milestone Pricing
lessons.what_is_taught: Designing milestone pricing: multi-phase work breakdown, deliverable-based milestones, milestone payment values, completion verification, and reconciling milestone sums to project price.
topics: Reconciling milestone sums to total project price

lessons.title: Milestone Payment Schedule
lessons.what_is_taught: Structuring payment schedules: upfront deposit requirements, milestone invoice triggers, client acceptance periods, payment terms, and project-specific cash-flow assumptions.

lessons.title: Recurring Service Pricing
lessons.what_is_taught: Modeling recurring retainer services: monthly billing cycles, recurring deliverable batches, allocated service capacity, reporting cadences, and additional work billing.

lessons.title: Retainer Boundaries
lessons.what_is_taught: Establishing sustainable retainer boundaries: included deliverables, hours caps, carryover policies, client availability windows, response times, and additional request protocols.
topics: Defining included hours and deliverable caps

lessons.title: Revision Allowances
lessons.what_is_taught: Defining revision allowances: number of revision rounds included, defining what constitutes a revision vs new scope, revision feedback windows, and hourly rates for extra revisions.
topics: Defining revisions vs new scope requests

lessons.title: Assumptions
lessons.what_is_taught: Documenting operational assumptions: client provision of brand assets, timely approvals within agreed windows, credential access, stable scope, and third-party fee responsibilities.
topics: Client provision of source files and assets

lessons.title: Exclusions
lessons.what_is_taught: Specifying explicit exclusions: services not covered, third-party stock/plugin licensing fees, scope expansion, ongoing maintenance, extra revisions, and rush delivery fees.
topics: Third-party software, fonts, and stock assets

lessons.title: Scope Changes
lessons.what_is_taught: Managing scope modifications: acknowledging change requests, written impact assessment, calculating cost and timeline adjustments, securing client approval, and updating project agreements.

lessons.title: Statement of Work Fundamentals
lessons.what_is_taught: Writing a professional Statement of Work (SOW): project background, detailed scope, deliverables specifications, schedule, responsibilities, assumptions, acceptance criteria, and change procedures.
topics: Purpose and role of the Statement of Work

lessons.title: SOW vs Legal Contract
lessons.what_is_taught: Understanding legal boundaries: SOW as a commercial scope document, incorporation into master services agreements, commercial obligations, and the role of independent legal counsel.
topics: SOW as a commercial scope document
How SOWs attach to master service agreements
Identifying when legal counsel is required

lessons.title: Pricing Risk Review
lessons.what_is_taught: Conducting pricing risk audits: identifying underestimated hours, ambiguous scope risks, unpriced work, currency fluctuations, platform fees, taxes, and payment gateway costs.
topics: Currency exchange risk on international work
